headline: Wall Street banks have reportedly begun selling parts of a record $60 billion debt package that funds Anthropic's leasing of AI chips.
score_reason: Pool score 6 kept: a record chip-financing deal reported by the Financial Times from people familiar with it, with the riskier part not yet on sale.
importance_line: Banks and investors that lend to AI companies, and Anthropic's chip orders for 2027, depend on how this sale goes, and the doubt is that the riskier $18 billion part is not yet on sale and may wait until after Anthropic's share listing.
summary: The Financial Times reports, as relayed by Investing.com, that Bank of America, Citigroup and Morgan Stanley started on Monday to offer other banks parts of a record $60 billion debt package that backs AI company Anthropic's lease of Google chips, beginning with $42 billion of loans supported by chip maker Broadcom's credit rating. This follows the Bloomberg report in our 3 Oct 2026 edition that banks had begun gathering the money; the new fact is that selling has started, while the riskier $18 billion part, with Blackstone committed to about $9 billion, is expected later and may wait until after Anthropic's planned share listing.
notes: FT page paywalled (HTTP 403). Text read in Investing.com's summary of the FT report on Yahoo Finance (https://finance.yahoo.com/technology/ai/articles/wall-street-tests-lender-appetite-214705266.html); Breakingthenews.net says the FT cites people familiar with the matter. FT link kept without its syn-25a6b1a6=1 syndication parameter. Follow-up of our 3 Oct 2026 item (Bloomberg, 2 Oct, banks starting to gather $60 billion).
